contradictions.detail: results[0].cost_tokens.mean is 0.0 (a fabricated-looking 0), but run_health/model_cost_by_variant record real token counts (recomputed mean 447693.0 tokens from [447430, 453343, 442306]). This is an instrumentation gap in RunMetrics.cost_tokens (the effort-budget token wiring is inert -- see run_ablation_live.py's _run_one docstring), NOT evidence that 0 tokens were actually spent.

run_health.breaker_failures = [2, 0, 2] (2 of 3 repeats hit circuit-breaker failures), but the log/report footer states 'no run was starved -- every row above is a clean, breaker-healthy measurement.' 'not starved' (true: starved=False and breaker_ended_open=False for every repeat) is a narrower claim than 'breaker-healthy' / 'no run starved' as used in BENCHMARK_REPORT.md's top-line status -- a breaker that recorded failures without opening is not the same as a run with zero failures.

BENCHMARK_REPORT.md cites wall/run=1330.0s for PixelMart, which matches one individual repeat's raw wall_time_s (1330.3394s) -- NOT the recomputed 3-run mean (1138.631s). The report appears to cite a single repeat instead of the mean across repeats.

blindtarget2.control_unit: recall: exchange (confirmed_vuln/confirmed_secure/inconclusive coarse ground truth). Precision: TWO units are both reported -- 'controls_clean' is per-EXCHANGE (any finding at all on a confirmed_secure exchange makes it dirty); 'controls_clean_issue_level'/'dirty_controls' is per (method+URL, vulnerability_class) ISSUE pair on that same exchange.
blindtarget2.recall_semantics: recall_any_finding = any finding present on a confirmed_vuln exchange; recall_surfaced_only = at least one of those findings was surfaced, not quarantined as a lead. Neither is exact-class recall -- no manifest backs this corpus.
